display.purpose: Hero and statement lines. Uppercase Montserrat Black, usually split so one clause lands in gold.

headline.purpose: Section headlines that make an argument. Light-weight Merriweather at large size — the brand's most recognisable typographic move.

title.purpose: Card and list-item headings. Tracked uppercase Montserrat Bold.

body.purpose: Reading copy at 1.8 line-height. Broken by line rather than justified into a block.

tagline.purpose: Brand lines only. Merriweather light italic, tracked and uppercased.

label.purpose: The tracked uppercase eyebrow above every section, and button text.

motion.name: ease-settle
motion.purpose: Arrivals that decelerate into place — panel reveals, slab openings.

motion.name: ease-strike
motion.purpose: GSAP easing for clip-path wipes, where copy is struck onto the page rather than faded in.

motion.name: ease-standard
motion.purpose: Default easing for state transitions and hover strikes.

motion.name: ease-overshoot
motion.purpose: Countdown-page digit drop only. Overshoot is otherwise out of system — the brand's motion constraint rules out bounce easing, and the homepage's emphasis word was moved onto ease-settle. Do not reach for this on new work.

motion.name: duration-reveal
motion.purpose: Scroll-triggered section reveals, staggered ~0.09s per item.

motion.name: scrub-tau
motion.purpose: Time constant for the cinematic field's scroll smoothing — how long the sky takes to catch up to the scrollbar.

components.name: Primary Button
components.description: The site's one hard action. Square by doctrine, magnetic to the pointer in the real implementation.

components.name: Text CTA
components.description: Used where a filled button would be too loud for the section.

components.name: Section Eyebrow
components.description: The tracked uppercase label that opens every section. Cheap, and it does most of the work of rhythm.
components.css: .ds-eyebrow { margin: 0; color: #e6b325; font-family: Montserrat, Arial, sans-serif; font-size: 0.75rem; font-weight: 500; letter-spacing: 0.35em; text-transform: uppercase; }

components.name: Marked Phrase
components.description: The signature device. The phrase a reader should leave with — never more than one per paragraph.
components.html: Bringing branding, advertising, marketing, events and performance under one roof.
components.css: .ds-marked-line { margin: 0; color: rgba(249,247,242,0.8); font-family: Montserrat, Arial, sans-serif; font-size: 1.5rem; font-weight: 300; line-height: 1.8; } .ds-marked { background: rgba(230,179,37,0.18); color: #e6b325; border-radius: 0.3em; padding: 0.04em 0.22em; -webkit-box-decoration-break: clone; box-decoration-break: clone; }

components.name: Copy Panel

components.name: Split Headline
components.description: The most transferable device in the identity: every headline divides into a quiet clause and a loud one.

narrative.overview:
The site is one continuous descent, not a stack of pages. A single dark field runs behind everything from the first viewport to the last; the scrollbar is a dolly track and the sections are transparent panes of type that the camera passes through. Nothing paints a ground of its own. That is the whole system in one sentence, and every other rule here exists to protect it.

This is a deliberate reversal of an earlier direction, and the reversal is binding. The project's original design language called for full-bleed colour blocks — "section = colour decision" — alternating navy, gold and white. Built out, every one of those edges read as the end of one page and the start of another. Colour blocking is now a confirmed anti-reference: it is the thing this system was defined against, and the ember accent that belonged to it is dropped from the palette entirely.

Type is the primary graphic. There are no icon sets, no illustration, no decorative furniture. The only ornament is light — gold bloom, beams, shader haze — and hairline rules. Restraint is the point: the brand's own thesis is "attention is rented, memory is owned", and a system that shouts on every section has nothing left to say on the one that matters.
keyCharacteristics: One continuous dark ground; sections are transparent panes, never blocks.
Montserrat and Merriweather, and nothing else.
Gold is a light source, not a fill — it marks the one thing that matters.
Depth is made with luminance and parallax, never with shadow.
Every section carries one interaction, in service of continuity.
Copy is dry, confident and slightly rude; the type setting matches.

rules.name: The One Light Rule
rules.body: Gold is a light source, not a fill. On any given viewport there is one thing lit in gold — one CTA, one marked phrase, one beam. Two golds competing on a screen means neither is the answer.

rules.name: The No Ground Rule
rules.body: No section paints a background. If a section needs separation, it gets space, a hairline, or a change in the camera — never a colour block. This is the single most load-bearing rule in the system.

rules.name: The Gold-on-White Ban
rules.body: Gold never sits on a light ground as text: not body, not links, not labels, not validation. On a light surface gold may only be a filled surface, a rule ≥4px, or display type ≥60px treated consciously as a decorative graphic whose accessible name comes from elsewhere.

rules.name: The Split Headline Rule
rules.body: Every display headline divides into a quiet clause and a loud clause — weight, colour or face carries the split. This is the most transferable device in the identity; a headline set in one uniform voice is a missed one.

rules.name: The Two Faces Rule
rules.body: Montserrat and Merriweather. A third family, a condensed cut, or a display face for one section is out of system.

rules.name: The Eyebrow Rule
rules.body: Every section opens with a tracked uppercase label in gold. It costs almost nothing and it does most of the work of rhythm.

rules.name: The Air, Not Edges Rule
rules.body: Separation between sections is space. If two sections read as running together, the fix is more vertical rhythm, never a background, a border, or a divider across the full width.

rules.name: The Light, Not Shadow Rule
rules.body: Depth is luminance and parallax. box-shadow is not a depth device here. If an element needs to lift off the page, light it or move it, don't drop a shadow under it.

rules.name: The Scrim Discipline Rule
rules.body: A scrim exists to make type legible over an active background, and it is always the lightest one that achieves that. A scrim heavy enough to flatten the effect underneath it has defeated the purpose of having the effect.

rules.name: The Square CTA Rule
rules.body: The primary action is never rounded. Rounding it makes it look like every other site's button, which is precisely the thing the brand has decided not to be.

dos: Do let the cinematic field be the only ground. Sections are transparent.
Do separate sections with vertical rhythm (7rem / 10rem) and hairlines at cream/15.
Do split every display headline into a quiet clause and a loud one.
Do keep gold to one lit thing per viewport.
Do set the primary CTA as a square gold block with charcoal text.
Do give a marked phrase box-decoration-break: clone so it survives a wrap.
Do gate every new shader on viewport proximity; the WebGL context budget is a real constraint on this page.
Do keep scroll-revealed content in the DOM pre-animation — animate opacity and transform only, never display: none.
Do design the prefers-reduced-motion variant as a composed static state, not an absence.
donts: Don't paint a section background or alternate colour blocks. This is the system's confirmed anti-reference, not a matter of taste.
Don't introduce an ember or any third accent. Gold is the only accent.
Don't load a third typeface, a condensed cut, or a display face for one section.
Don't use box-shadow as a depth device.
Don't set gold as text on a light ground, at any size, for anything meant to be read.
Don't stack two interactions in one section, or repeat the same effect across sections — motion serves continuity, and an effect that calls attention to itself as an effect works against it.
Don't let a scrim get heavy enough to flatten the effect it sits over.
Don't add icon sets, illustration, or decorative furniture. Type and light are the graphics.
